newsitem.title: USA: Yankee Energy offering to lease fuel cells.
newsitem.headline: Yankee Energy offering to lease fuel cells.

text.p: Yankee Energy Services Co, is offering to lease fuel cells or install and operate the units as part of an energy sales program that charges the customer for the energy consumed as electricity or heat, YESCo market planning director Steve Pesutti said Wednesday.
As part of an energy sales program, YESCo would provide the fuel, either from the open market or its Yankee Gas Services Co affiliate, Pesutti explained.

Without federal subsidies, he said, the fuel cells are able to provide power at a cost of $0.12 to $0.14 per kilowatt hour without any credit for the heat provided. The subsidies are expected to reduce this to $0.10 to $0.12 per KWH, and one project is coming in between $0.085 and $0.09 per KWH.

A fuel cell uses an electrochemical process to directly convert chemical energy into electricity and hot water. The chemical energy normally comes from hydrogen contained in natural gas. However, fuel cells do not burn the gas so they operate virtually pollution-free.

Asked about how these units are being treated by the local utilities, Pesutti said most of the customers YESCo is dealing with are buying power under the small commercial tarrif, which makes no provision for stand-by power.

In order to get the heat needed to heat buildings at night, when there is little electricity demand in the building where the fuel cell is installed, he said, Northeast Utilities' Connecticut Light & Power Co is installing reverse meters, allowing the building to sell unneeded electricity to the utility.
